theFindingTheProbeMade.whatTheFirstProbeSaid: Round Rock (Williamson 48491, the point at the City Hall) served `etjStatus: absent` on all 6 nearest parcels, against a pre-registered prediction of `unresolved`.
theFindingTheProbeMade.whyThatIsWrong: round-rock-tx is in the register as mode=city_limits_only with has_etj_rings=false: it publishes NO ETJ layer at all. `absent` there claims a verified absence of ETJ for a city whose ETJ was never published. Austin's published ETJ extent box happens to cover Round Rock, so the extent-box fallback answered 'austin-tx covers this point and none of its rings contains it' -- true about Austin, false as the aggregate disposition. P-241's own surface probe answered `unresolved` for the same city, so two instruments on one premise disagreed: a free finding (DEV_PROCESS).
theFindingTheProbeMade.rootCause: the overlay passed `containing` only when the city-limits answer was `incorporated`; every other answer (in practice `unmeasured`, and refusals, which this rail serves as `unmeasured`) meant `containing: null`, and `resolveEtjAtPoint` then applies its documented box fallback -- which its own header says is only valid for a point KNOWN to be unincorporated.
theFindingTheProbeMade.theFix: a box-rule `absent` is now only served when the city-limits answer SETTLED the containing city: 'incorporated' (names it, passed through) or 'unincorporated' (positively says there is none). Otherwise the miss is kept, its coveredBy and ringsConsulted travel, and the disposition is `unresolved` with a basis that names the unread containing city. `present` is untouched: a ring containment never depended on the containing city.
theFindingTheProbeMade.testThatPinsIt: FALSIFIER 1c in cityLimitsFactServeCutover.test.ts ('an extent-box miss with the containing city UNREAD stays unresolved'), plus the ring-containment-is-branch-independent case. Both fail if the rule is removed.
theFindingTheProbeMade.consequenceDeclaredPlainly: In any process whose city-limits answer is not a positive determination, `absent` is now unreachable and the miss reads `unresolved`. That is a deliberate loss of a flattering number in exchange for never printing a verified absence over an unpublished ETJ. The live parcel legs of falsifier 1 show exactly that, row by row, rather than hiding it.

productionPathAndCommands.decision: A SESSION CLI run under a heavy-scan lease keyed on the production HOST -- not a Cloud Run job.
why: Scope of the freeze: _decisions/2026-08-26_ingest_freeze_and_cloud_loader.md freezes 'Factory 1 atoms ingest from the operator's PC' -- the ATOMS store path, re-engineered as a Cloud Run job (P-81..P-84). It does not name deployment-store boundary tables, and ETJ rings are not atoms.

Where the code lives: etjCli/etjIngest are LDT `lib/cad-ingest` CLIs, exposed as `pnpm --filter @workspace/cad-ingest etj-ingest` / `etj-verify`. There is no factory job, image or service account that carries them; a Cloud Run job would need all three built first, for a job that takes 34.1s for 20 publishers.

Precedent for exactly this shape: the immediately preceding production write of the same class -- apply 0103 BY HAND with its tracker row under a production lease, then run the Austin zoning stamp from a session (A-207 ruling 3; A-202 for session-run stamps against production; recorded in _inbox/2026-09-16_texas_scaleup_ROADMAP.md's P-259b row) -- is a session under a lease, and the dispatch hands the same job to the integration seat.

It is a full-table writer to two tables (deletes what it re-acquires, then batch-upserts), so ONE heavy-scan scope and the single-writer rule bind. The lease is keyed on the HOST, never a nickname (P-307).

whatTheBuildTaughtThatThePlanDidNot.LESSON: An `absent` from a publisher's published extent box is only a verified absence when the containing city is SETTLED. A city that publishes no ETJ layer (mode=city_limits_only) sitting inside a neighbour's extent box is the exact shape that turns 'we have no source here' into 'there is no ETJ here'. Any future consumer of loadEtjFact must answer the containing-city question first, or pass `containing`; the wrapper now enforces that by construction, but the same trap is open to the next caller. Pinned by FALSIFIER 1c.

The staged/slated city-limits branch reads parcel_record through the retrieval service, so in a process without RETRIEVAL_API_KEY every slated county answers `unmeasured`. A probing process that lacks that credential cannot demonstrate a checked absence in 48453/48021/48491 at all -- which means ANY future probe of a slated rail must declare its credential state up front or its numbers will be read as a data finding.
whatTheBuildTaughtThatThePlanDidNot.GROUND-TRUTH: LDT staging (ep-gentle-star-appmbu2q.c-7.us-east-1.aws.neon.tech) carries 355 ETJ rings, 23 register rows, 20 publishers with rings and 3 city_limits_only (cedar-park-tx, lockhart-tx, round-rock-tx), ingested 2026-09-17T18:05:23Z..18:05:56Z, `_schema_migrations` holding one 0102 row. Verified by SELECT at 19:2x Z.
The shared staging database was RESET by another session's schema operation mid-lane (tx_etj_source vanished). Any lane relying on staging rows should re-verify presence, not vintage.
whatTheBuildTaughtThatThePlanDidNot.DEAD-END: `psql` against the staging URL is the fastest verification and the only one that survived the LAN; the earlier `heavy-scan-lease list` through node on this box crashed the node process at exit (uv async assertion) AFTER printing correct JSON -- the operation succeeded and the crash is a runner artifact, so do not read a non-zero exit there as a failed lease call.
`pnpm install` / any pnpm script on this box needs Git's sh on PATH (`C:\Program Files\Git\bin`, `C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin`); without it pnpm dies with `sh: not recognized`.

`pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` inside artifacts/api-server alone reports hundreds of TS6305 'output file ... has not been built' errors. The repo's root `pnpm run typecheck` builds the project references first and is the CI-shaped command; the per-artifact form is not a usable local signal.
whatTheBuildTaughtThatThePlanDidNot.OPEN: hauska-engine's `report-model.ts:966` and `pdf/feasibility.ts:210-212` still hardcode ETJ for the report and PDF surfaces. They are named in the dispatch as another lane's work and were not touched; until they adopt the same read, the card/MCP and the PDF can disagree about ETJ.

The `etj` rail in parcelConstraintProjection is still declared-ahead/unread on every row, so any filter over the ETJ column refuses. Serving it needs a query point in the projection path, which is a different design question than this lane's overlay.
